scenes.tts: Picture two cells that touch. One carries a B type ephrin, held in its membrane. The other carries its receptor. When the two proteins bind, the receptor signals into its own cell. That is the forward signal. A second message passes into the ephrin's cell. That is reverse signaling. Now suppose you delete the gene for the ephrin, and an organ fails to form. What did you take away?

scenes.visual: Two cells, the receptor above gripping the ephrin below. The ephrin disappears and the grip opens; an organ chip appears and is crossed out; a question mark sits in the gap.
scenes.narration: Picture two cells that touch. One carries a B-type ephrin, held in its membrane. The other carries its receptor. When the two proteins bind, the receptor signals into its own cell. That is the forward signal. A second message passes into the ephrin's cell. That is reverse signaling. Now suppose you delete the gene for the ephrin, and an organ fails to form. What did you take away?

scenes.tts: You have removed the forward signal into the receptor's cell. You have also removed the reverse signal into the ephrin's cell. And you have removed the plain grip that held the two cells together.
scenes.caption: You have removed the forward signal into the receptor's cell. You have also removed the reverse signal into the ephrin's cell. And you have removed the plain grip that held the two cells together.
scenes.visual: Same picture. A dashed green arrow and label (forward signal) in the upper cell is crossed out; a dashed orange arrow and label (reverse signal) in the lower cell is crossed out; then the word grip beside the gap is crossed out.
scenes.narration: You have removed the forward signal into the receptor's cell. You have also removed the reverse signal into the ephrin's cell. And you have removed the plain grip that held the two cells together.

scenes.tts: Deleting the receptor has the same problem. Its outer part was a ligand for the other cell. So here too, one deletion cannot say which loss mattered.
scenes.caption: Deleting the receptor has the same problem. Its outer part was a ligand for the other cell. So here too, one deletion cannot say which loss mattered.
scenes.visual: The ephrin returns and the pair grips again. The receptor vanishes. Before it goes, its outer part is labelled and marked as a ligand for the other cell. A question mark sits at the gap.
scenes.narration: Deleting the receptor has the same problem. Its outer part was a ligand for the other cell. So here too, one deletion cannot say which loss mattered.

scenes.tts: The knockout cannot tell you which loss caused the defect. The failed organ does not say which. So here is a design problem for you. How could we disrupt reverse signaling while leaving forward signaling intact? Design the mouse, or the reagent, for an ephrin of the B class.

scenes.visual: Three chips (forward signal, reverse signal, grip) point at a crossed-out organ with a question mark: which one? Then the design problem is written below, unanswered.
